title: Separate record identity from content identity
summary: Use a stable record identifier and an explicit revision; a digest identifies bytes, not permission or durability.
objectives: Distinguish application identity, revision and content digest.
Recognize that serialization is part of a digest contract.

sources.title: JSON Canonicalization Scheme
sources.basis: Describes invariant serialization for reproducible digest/signature inputs; the exercise is not a JCS implementation.

sections.title: The same record can have different content
paragraphs: A synthetic record keeps its identifier while its revision and body change. A digest of the old body does not identify the new bytes.
Hash comparison alone establishes neither storage durability nor permission to read or publish the record.

sections.title: Specify the representation
paragraphs: JSON objects with different property order can serialize to different bytes. Use a specified representation when a protocol needs canonical identity; do not invent a cryptographic encoding from this exercise.
Missing linked content is an explicit missing result, not an empty record or invented content.

exercise.instruction: Run the selected-knowledge exercises with pnpm test.
exercise.expected: Assert the documented result and its negative boundary; no external operation is performed.

limitations: The exercise compares fixed UTF-8 strings with the platform hash implementation. It does not implement JCS, a content-addressed store or a permission system.
